7	"Phase 3 detail", requirements 1 to 7. Evidence:
8	`~/code/ai-lawnmower/ralph/plans/lm-steer-design/results.md`, numbered checks.
9	Both are outside this repository and are read-only; the facts they supply are
10	transcribed in [research.md](research.md) and in
11	`ralph/plans/lm-steer-crswd-018/PROGRESS.md`.
12	
13	**Spec**: this file · **Research**: [research.md](research.md) ·
14	**Plan**: [plan.md](plan.md) · **Tasks**: [tasks.md](tasks.md)
15	
16	`POST /sessions/{id}/prompt` is the one API route that delivers free text into a
17	running session. ai-lawnmower calls it today — a board answer, a requeue resume,
18	an opp-lease batch handoff, an opp-lease follow-up — so every requirement below
19	is a change to a live route with a live client. Nothing here adds a route,
20	a `tmuxctl.Controller` method or a package.
21	
22	Every decision this specification rests on was taken before it was written and is
23	recorded with its evidence in [research.md](research.md) as D1 to D9. This file
24	states what must be true; research.md states why, and what was rejected.
25	
26	## User Scenarios & Testing *(mandatory)*
27	
28	### User Story 1 - A prompt into a session that is no longer running is refused, not executed (Priority: P1)
29	
30	A script sends a prompt to a session whose Claude Code has exited while its tmux
31	window survived. Today the text lands in the login shell underneath and the Enter
32	after it runs the first line as a command, unsandboxed, as the daemon's user. The
33	caller is told `202 delivered`. After this feature the daemon refuses, nothing
34	reaches the pane, and the caller is told so in a form it already understands.
35	
36	**Why this priority**: it is the one failure in this route that executes caller
37	text as a host command line. Everything else here is correctness; this is the
38	security gate.
39	
40	**Independent Test**: put a session's pane on a shell with `@crswd-binary` still
41	naming `claude`, POST a prompt, and read the pane back: `409`, and the pane is
42	empty.
43	
44	**Acceptance Scenarios**:
45	
46	1. **Given** a session whose pane command no longer matches `@crswd-binary`,
47	   **When** a prompt is posted, **Then** the answer is `409`
48	   `{"error":"session not ready"}`, no tmux command that changes anything has
49	   run, and the audit record is a Deny whose reason is `session not ready`.
50	2. **Given** a session whose Claude exits **between** the paste and the submit,
51	   **When** the prompt is delivered, **Then** the daemon sends `C-u`, sends no
52	   Enter, and answers `409`. Nothing runs in the shell.
53	3. **Given** a session whose liveness is unknown — created by a build older than
54	   `@crswd-binary` — **When** a prompt is posted, **Then** it is delivered, as the
55	   supervisor already treats that state as healthy.
56	4. **Given** a controller `List` that fails, **When** a prompt is posted, **Then**
57	   the answer is the route's existing `500` with no detail, and nothing is
58	   delivered. A readiness check that cannot run is not a readiness check that
59	   passed.
60	
61	---
62	
63	### User Story 2 - A prompt into a session the supervisor gave up on is refused (Priority: P1)
64	
65	A session in state `failed` is one the supervisor tried to revive and ran out of
66	attempts for. Nothing is running in its pane. A prompt into it is the same failure
67	as User Story 1 reached by a different road, and it gets the same answer.
68	
69	**Why this priority**: it is the same host exposure, and it is one comparison.
70	
71	**Independent Test**: POST a prompt to a session recorded `failed`; the answer is
72	`409` and the fake controller recorded no command at all.
73	
74	**Acceptance Scenarios**:
75	
76	1. **Given** a session in state `failed`, **When** a prompt is posted, **Then**
77	   the answer is `409` `{"error":"session not ready"}` and no tmux command ran.
78	2. **Given** a session in state `dead`, **When** a prompt is posted, **Then** the
79	   answer is exactly what it is today — the resolver's uniform `404` — and this
80	   feature changes nothing about it.
81	
82	---
83	
84	### User Story 3 - A multi-line prompt arrives once, whole, as text (Priority: P1)
85	
86	The opp-lease handoff sends a multi-line item body. Under a plain paste a harness
87	can submit line one early and treat the rest as a second turn. A bracketed paste
88	is the form both harnesses read as one block of text.
89	
90	**Why this priority**: it is the correctness half of the requirement that the
91	route carries what the caller wrote, and lawnmower's real payloads are multi-line.
92	
93	**Independent Test**: deliver a two-line prompt and assert one bracketed paste
94	followed by exactly one Enter — against the fake, and against a real tmux pane
95	running `cat`.
96	
97	**Acceptance Scenarios**:
98	
99	1. **Given** a Claude session, **When** a two-line prompt is delivered, **Then**
100	   the controller recorded one `PasteBracketed` and one Enter, in that order, and
101	   no plain `Paste`.
102	2. **Given** a Codex session, **When** a prompt is delivered, **Then** it is also
103	   bracketed. `Prompt` no longer asks which harness it is talking to.
104	3. **Given** a compact, **When** it is delivered, **Then** it still uses the
105	   harness-based paste it uses today. Its payload is a daemon constant.
106	4. **Given** a prompt holding `ESC [ 2 0 1 ~`, **When** it is posted, **Then** it
107	   is refused with `400` and nothing reaches the pane (FR-007).
108	
109	---
110	
111	### User Story 4 - A prompt that is really a command is refused (Priority: P2)
112	
113	A client that meant to say something and instead sent `/clear` discards the
114	conversation it was trying to continue; one that sent `!rm -rf …` runs a shell
115	command in the session's own unsandboxed context. On the API door those two
116	leading characters are a client bug, and the daemon can see it.
117	
118	**Why this priority**: it is cheap, it is decided at the boundary, and no measured
119	caller is refused by it. It ranks below the three above because a client has to
120	send it deliberately.
121	
122	**Independent Test**: POST `"/clear"`; the answer is `400` and the fake recorded
123	nothing. POST the same text through the browser type route; it is delivered.
124	
125	**Acceptance Scenarios**:
126	
127	1. **Given** a prompt whose first non-whitespace character is `/` or `!`, **When**
128	   it is posted to the API door, **Then** the answer is `400` with the uniform
129	   bad-request body and no tmux command ran.
130	2. **Given** a prompt whose *later* line begins with `/`, **When** it is posted,
131	   **Then** it is delivered. The rule reads the first non-whitespace character of
132	   the whole text and nothing else.
133	3. **Given** the operator typing `/compact` into the session page's input panel,
134	   **When** they press Send, **Then** it is delivered unchanged. The browser door
135	   is not touched by this rule.
136	
137	---
138	
139	### User Story 5 - Two writers cannot interleave inside one pane (Priority: P2)
140	
141	A prompt that arrives while a revive or a continue is typing a new command line
142	into the pane lands partly in the dying process and partly in the next one. The
143	session lock does not exclude a restart, because a restart does not hold it for
144	its whole run.
145	
146	**Why this priority**: it is a real corruption, and it is rare — it needs a prompt
147	to arrive inside a restart's window.
148	
149	**Independent Test**: hold the restart claim, POST a prompt, and see `409` with no
150	tmux command recorded.
151	
152	**Acceptance Scenarios**:
153	
154	1. **Given** a revive or continue holding the session's restart claim, **When** a
155	   prompt is posted, **Then** the answer is `409` `{"error":"session not ready"}`
156	   and no tmux command ran. The prompt does not wait for the restart.
157	2. **Given** two prompts to one session at the same moment, **When** both run,
158	   **Then** each uses its own tmux buffer name and neither one's Enter lands
159	   between the other's paste and Enter.
160	
161	---
162	
163	### User Story 6 - A caller can find its own delivery in the trail (Priority: P3)
164	
165	A client that delivered a prompt and then lost its answer — a timeout, a daemon
166	restart — has no way to tell whether the text landed. The audit trail is the only
167	durable record of a delivery, and today it carries nothing the caller chose.
168	
169	**Why this priority**: it is an operability feature, not a safety one, and it is
170	the only requirement here that adds a field rather than a refusal.
171	
172	**Independent Test**: POST with `"request_id":"abc-123"`; the `202` echoes it and
173	the audit record carries it. POST a 33-character or upper-case one; `400`.
174	
175	**Acceptance Scenarios**:
176	
177	1. **Given** a body carrying a valid `request_id`, **When** the prompt is
178	   delivered, **Then** the `202` echoes the value and the request's one audit
179	   record carries it in a field named `request_id`.
180	2. **Given** a body carrying an invalid `request_id`, **When** it arrives,
181	   **Then** the answer is `400` and no tmux command ran.
182	3. **Given** a body carrying no `request_id`, **When** the prompt is delivered,
183	   **Then** the field appears nowhere — not in the response, not on the record.
184	   An existing client sees byte-for-byte the response it sees today.
185	4. **Given** a refused prompt that carried a valid `request_id`, **When** it is
186	   refused, **Then** the Deny record carries the same field.
187	
188	---
189	
190	### Edge Cases
191	
192	- **A prompt holding `ESC [ 2 0 1 ~`.** Under today's plain paste the bytes are
193	  inert; under FR-005's bracketed paste they would end the paste early and the
194	  remainder would reach the pane as keystrokes. FR-007 refuses the payload, so it
195	  cannot arrive. This is the one exposure bracketing *creates*, and it is closed
196	  in the same change that creates it.
197	- **A prompt holding a bare `\r`.** Refused by FR-007 as a C0 control. This door
198	  does not CRLF-normalise the way the session page's route does: the API door's
199	  text is delivered byte-for-byte, and rewriting it here would deliver something
200	  the caller did not send. No measured caller sends one.
201	- **A prompt between 16 KiB and the body bound.** Delivered. FR-007 adopts the
202	  character rule and deliberately **not** the session page's 16384-byte bound; the
203	  prompt route keeps the body bound it has today.
204	- **A later line beginning `/` or `!`.** Delivered (FR-008). The `resume.txt`
205	  fixture holds a line beginning `/compact` for exactly this reason.
206	- **A pane that falls back to a shell between the second liveness read and the
207	  Enter.** Not covered, and not claimed to be: the window is two tmux commands
208	  wide and nothing measured it (research.md "Not verified").
209	- **A Codex composer meeting the `C-u` of FR-003.** `C-u` clears a Claude composer
210	  and a shell line; Codex's was not measured. The worst case is a composer left
211	  holding text that was never submitted, which is the state a refused prompt is
212	  supposed to leave behind.
213	- **A session parked on a dialog.** Still accepts a prompt. `parked_on` and
214	  `suspicious_dialog` keep reporting it in the `202` and keep not refusing — the
215	  readiness signal that would refuse it is out of scope (D8).
216	- **A `request_id` reused by the caller.** The daemon does not deduplicate. It is a
217	  correlation value the caller chose, not a key the daemon owns, and a route that
218	  remembered one would be keeping state about callers it deliberately keeps none
219	  about.
220	
221	## Requirements *(mandatory)*
222	
223	### Readiness
224	
225	- **FR-001**: `Manager.Prompt` MUST read the session's row from the controller's
226	  `List` before any tmux command that changes anything, and branch on its `Claude`
227	  liveness: `LivenessStopped` refuses, `LivenessUnknown` and `LivenessRunning`
228	  deliver, and a `List` that fails is an error and never a delivery. It MUST NOT
229	  add a method to `tmuxctl.Controller`, so the `k8s/` module's `podctl` is
230	  untouched.
231	- **FR-002**: Readiness MUST NOT be decided by reading what the pane shows. Spec
232	  012 FR-007 forbids it for detection and pane content is secret under
233	  `docs/security.md` §3; `paneDialogState` stays what it is, additive information
234	  and never a gate.
235	- **FR-003**: `Manager.Prompt` MUST read liveness a second time after the paste and
236	  before the Enter. If that read is `LivenessStopped` it MUST send `C-u`, MUST NOT
237	  send Enter, and MUST refuse. No third read is required: the lost-Enter window
238	  measured by the probe is the first seconds after launch, which is out of scope.
239	- **FR-004**: `Manager.Prompt` MUST refuse a session in state `failed` before any
240	  tmux command. A session in state `dead` keeps today's answer unchanged.
241	
242	### The refusal
243	
244	- **FR-005**: `internal/session` MUST gain exactly one sentinel,
245	  `ErrSessionNotReady`, and every refusal FR-001, FR-003, FR-004 and FR-010 make
246	  MUST return it. `refusePrompt` MUST map it to `409` with body
247	  `{"error":"session not ready"}`, and the request's one audit record MUST be a
248	  Deny whose reason is the constant `session not ready`. That reason names no
249	  state, no pane content and no prompt. No other status, body or reason is added
250	  to this route.
251	
252	### Delivery
253	
254	- **FR-006**: `Manager.Prompt` MUST deliver with `PasteBracketed` for every
255	  harness — one paste, then at most one Enter. `Manager.Compact` MUST keep the
256	  harness-based paste it uses today; its payload is a daemon constant, not caller
257	  text. No rule refusing newlines may be added: the opp-lease handoff pastes
258	  multi-line bodies, and bracketing is what makes a newline safe.
259	- **FR-007**: Because FR-006 brackets this route's paste, the prompt text MUST be
260	  refused when it is not valid UTF-8, or holds any byte in `0x00–0x1F` other than
261	  `0x09` and `0x0A`, or holds `0x7F`. This is the rule `docs/security.md` §2
262	  already states for bracketed paste and `session.ValidateTyped` already applies
263	  for the session page (spec 018 FR-004), and it MUST be **the same predicate
264	  rather than a second copy** — two spellings of one rule are free to disagree,
265	  and the one that disagrees is the one nobody reads. The refusal MUST be `400`
266	  with the uniform bad-request body, before any tmux command.
267	  - The **length** half of `ValidateTyped` is deliberately not adopted. The prompt
268	    route keeps the bound it has today (`CRSW_MAX_BODY_BYTES`, default 65536);
269	    taking `MaxTypeBytes` (16384) with it would tighten a live route's bound for
270	    no requirement, which is a client break wearing a safety check's clothes.
271	  - This door MUST NOT CRLF-normalise. The session page's route rewrites `\r\n`
272	    before validating because a textarea produces it; the API door delivers caller
273	    bytes unaltered, so a `\r` is refused rather than rewritten.
274	- **FR-008**: The API door MUST refuse a prompt whose first character that is not
275	  space, tab, CR or LF is `!` or `/`, with `400` and the uniform bad-request body,
276	  before any tmux command. The rule reads the first non-whitespace character of
277	  the whole text and no other character. The session page's type route MUST be
278	  unchanged, and a test MUST assert that it still delivers `/compact`.
279	
280	### Concurrency
281	
282	- **FR-009**: `Manager.Prompt` MUST take the restart claim (`claimRestart`,
283	  non-blocking) **after** `lockSession`, and MUST release it on return. The order
284	  matches `Continue`'s, so no new lock ordering enters the package.
285	- **FR-010**: A prompt that finds the restart claim held MUST refuse with
286	  `ErrSessionNotReady` and MUST run no tmux command. It MUST NOT wait: a prompt
287	  that blocked across a process restart would hold the request open, and a caller
288	  cannot tell a slow delivery from a lost one.
289	- **FR-011**: The two guarantees already true MUST be asserted rather than assumed
290	  — the per-session mutex is held across the paste and the Enter together, and
291	  each paste draws its own tmux buffer name. A test MUST show two concurrent
292	  prompts using distinct buffer names and never interleaving a paste and a submit.
293	
294	### Correlation
295	
296	- **FR-012**: `promptRequest` MUST gain one optional field, `request_id`, of 1 to
297	  32 characters drawn from `[a-z0-9-]`. A value outside that is a `400` decided at
298	  the boundary, before any tmux command. The body stays decoded with
299	  `DisallowUnknownFields`, so no other new field is accepted.
300	- **FR-013**: A valid `request_id` MUST be echoed in the `202` body and written to
301	  the request's one audit record under the key `request_id`. An absent one MUST
302	  appear nowhere: the field is omitted from the response and from the record, so a
303	  client that sends none sees today's bytes.
304	- **FR-014**: The record MUST gain the `request_id` and **nothing about the
305	  prompt** — not its text, not its length, not a hash of it. `Record.Reason` stays
306	  server-authored sentinels and MUST NOT carry the value; `request_id` is the one
307	  field on the record whose bytes a caller chose.
308	
309	### Bounds on the change
310	
311	- **FR-015**: The API door MUST still have exactly six routes, and this feature
312	  MUST NOT add a package under `internal/`, a dependency, a `go.sum`, or a
313	  `tmuxctl.Controller` method.
314	- **FR-016**: Every payload shape ai-lawnmower sends today — board answer, requeue
315	  resume, opp-lease batch handoff, opp-lease follow-up — MUST still answer `202`
316	  with `"delivered":true`. The four are fixed byte-for-byte as test fixtures so
317	  that a later change to any rule here is measured against the traffic rather than
318	  argued about.
319	- **FR-017**: `docs/security.md` MUST gain a "Prompt route gates (spec 020)"
320	  subsection under "Non-negotiables", naming the liveness gate, the `failed`
321	  refusal, the bracketed paste and the control-character rule it brings, the
322	  leading-character rule, the restart claim and `request_id`. `AGENTS.md` MUST NOT
323	  be edited, and MUST stay under the 150-line CI limit.
324	
325	### Amendments to shipped specifications
326	
327	- **FR-018**: Spec 018 **FR-006** ("the API door's `POST /sessions/{id}/prompt`
328	  MUST be unchanged: plain paste, then Enter. Bracketed paste is for the
329	  interactive route only") is amended by FR-006, FR-007 and FR-008 of this
330	  specification: the route's paste becomes bracketed, it gains the
331	  control-character rule that bracketing makes load-bearing, and it gains one
332	  refusal the interactive route does not have. Nothing else about the interactive
333	  route changes, and spec 018's own FR-004 is untouched.
334	- **FR-019**: Spec 001 **FR-042** (an audit record carries no prompt text, no
335	  session output, no credential and no shared secret) is amended for exactly one
336	  field by FR-013 and FR-014: the record may carry a caller-supplied `request_id`
337	  of at most 32 characters from `[a-z0-9-]`. Everything else FR-042 forbids stays
338	  forbidden, and the alphabet is what keeps the field from becoming a channel for
339	  the text — 32 bytes of that set cannot carry a prompt.
340	
341	### Out of scope
342	
343	- **FR-020**: A readiness gate reading Claude Code's session registry
344	  (`sessions/<pid>.json`) is **not** built here. It was stated as a MAY; probe
345	  check 8 left open whether the daemon can read that file at all under spec 017's
346	  v2 option B, so a gate built on it would work on the VM and be blind in the
347	  cluster; and probe checks 3 and 9 show the registry misses the trust dialog and
348	  a half-typed draft, so it answers "a session exists" rather than "this session
349	  will read what I send next". Deferring a MAY is a decision, and research.md D8
350	  records it as one. The cost is stated there: a session parked on a dialog still
351	  accepts a prompt.
352	- **FR-021**: Also out of scope, each with its reason in research.md D9: opening a
353	  Claude transcript or registry file from Go (spec 013 FR-025 is unchanged);
354	  holding or calling an LLM; a seventh API route; free text on the browser door
355	  beyond spec 018; the startup lost-Enter window (probe check 1b); and the socket
356	  transport, which belongs to the lm-steer-write milestone.
357	
358	**Key Entities**: **Liveness**, the existing three-valued `tmuxctl` answer derived
359	from `@crswd-binary` against the pane's current command — running, stopped,
360	unknown. **Not-ready**, one condition with one sentinel and one answer, covering a
361	stopped pane, a `failed` session and a held restart claim; the caller cannot tell
362	the three apart because to a caller they are one event, *not now, try later*.
363	**`request_id`**, a caller-chosen correlation value, bounded in length and
364	alphabet, and the only caller bytes on an audit record.
365	
366	## Success Criteria *(mandatory)*
367	
368	- **SC-001**: `go test ./internal/... -run Prompt` proves, against the fake
369	  controller, each of: a stopped pane answers `409` `{"error":"session not ready"}`
370	  with no paste; a `failed` session the same with no tmux command at all; an exit
371	  between the paste and the Enter yields `C-u`, no Enter and `409`; a held restart
372	  claim yields `409` with no tmux command.
373	- **SC-002**: `go test -tags tmux ./internal/session/ -run Prompt` proves on a real
374	  tmux that a pane on `sh` carrying `@crswd-binary` `claude` is refused and reads
375	  back empty, and that a two-line prompt into `cat` arrives once.
376	- **SC-003**: `go test ./internal/httpapi/ -run 'Prompt|Type'` proves that a
377	  leading `/` or `!` answers `400` with nothing delivered, and that the session
378	  page's type route still delivers `/compact`.
379	- **SC-004**: `go test ./internal/httpapi/ -run RequestID` proves that a valid
380	  `request_id` is echoed and audited, that a 33-character or upper-case one answers
381	  `400` with nothing delivered, and that an absent one appears nowhere.
382	- **SC-005**: `go test ./internal/httpapi/ -run Lawnmower` posts all four fixtures
383	  and gets `202` `"delivered":true` for each.
384	- **SC-006**: The leak suite finds no prompt text, no length and no hash of it in
385	  any audit record or log line, with the new field present.
386	- **SC-007**: `grep -cE '^## \`(GET|POST|DELETE|PATCH|PUT) '
387	  specs/001-crswd-daemon-core/contracts/http-api.md` prints `6`, and a diff of
388	  `internal/`'s directories against `main` is empty.
389	- **SC-008**: `go test ./...`, `go test -tags tmux ./...`,
390	  `go vet -tags quickstart ./cmd/crswd` and `golangci-lint run` all exit 0, and
391	  `go.sum` still does not exist.
392	
393	## Assumptions
394	
395	- `@crswd-binary` against the pane's current command is a true liveness signal for
396	  the sessions this route serves. Probe check 13 measured 6 of 6 live panes,
397	  three of them `rcq`.
398	- ai-lawnmower is the only client of this route. The grep that found no caller
399	  refused by FR-008 covered that client; an unknown client sending a leading `/`,
400	  a control byte or a bare `\r` is refused with a `400` it can see and fix.
401	- `409 {"error":"session not ready"}` needs no client change: lawnmower's
402	  `deliver()` already treats any body carrying an `error` key as a refusal.
403	- A refusal is cheaper than a wrong delivery on this route, because a wrong
404	  delivery is a command line in an unsandboxed shell and a refusal is a retry.
405

# Feature Specification: Prompt Route Safety

**Feature Branch**: `plan/lm-steer-crswd-018`
**Created**: 2026-10-14
**Status**: Draft
**Input**: `~/code/ai-lawnmower/docs/mcp-session-steering-design.md`, section (g)
"Phase 3 detail", requirements 1 to 7. Evidence:
`~/code/ai-lawnmower/ralph/plans/lm-steer-design/results.md`, numbered checks.
Both are outside this repository and are read-only; the facts they supply are
transcribed in [research.md](research.md) and in
`ralph/plans/lm-steer-crswd-018/PROGRESS.md`.

**Spec**: this file · **Research**: [research.md](research.md) ·
**Plan**: [plan.md](plan.md) · **Tasks**: [tasks.md](tasks.md)

`POST /sessions/{id}/prompt` is the one API route that delivers free text into a
running session. ai-lawnmower calls it today — a board answer, a requeue resume,
an opp-lease batch handoff, an opp-lease follow-up — so every requirement below
is a change to a live route with a live client. Nothing here adds a route,
a `tmuxctl.Controller` method or a package.

Every decision this specification rests on was taken before it was written and is
recorded with its evidence in [research.md](research.md) as D1 to D9. This file
states what must be true; research.md states why, and what was rejected.

## User Scenarios & Testing *(mandatory)*

### User Story 1 - A prompt into a session that is no longer running is refused, not executed (Priority: P1)

A script sends a prompt to a session whose Claude Code has exited while its tmux
window survived. Today the text lands in the login shell underneath and the Enter
after it runs the first line as a command, unsandboxed, as the daemon's user. The
caller is told `202 delivered`. After this feature the daemon refuses, nothing
reaches the pane, and the caller is told so in a form it already understands.

**Why this priority**: it is the one failure in this route that executes caller
text as a host command line. Everything else here is correctness; this is the
security gate.

**Independent Test**: put a session's pane on a shell with `@crswd-binary` still
naming `claude`, POST a prompt, and read the pane back: `409`, and the pane is
empty.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** a session whose pane command no longer matches `@crswd-binary`,
   **When** a prompt is posted, **Then** the answer is `409`
   `{"error":"session not ready"}`, no tmux command that changes anything has
   run, and the audit record is a Deny whose reason is `session not ready`.
2. **Given** a session whose Claude exits **between** the paste and the submit,
   **When** the prompt is delivered, **Then** the daemon sends `C-u`, sends no
   Enter, and answers `409`. Nothing runs in the shell.
3. **Given** a session whose liveness is unknown — created by a build older than
   `@crswd-binary` — **When** a prompt is posted, **Then** it is delivered, as the
   supervisor already treats that state as healthy.
4. **Given** a controller `List` that fails, **When** a prompt is posted, **Then**
   the answer is the route's existing `500` with no detail, and nothing is
   delivered. A readiness check that cannot run is not a readiness check that
   passed.

---

### User Story 2 - A prompt into a session the supervisor gave up on is refused (Priority: P1)

A session in state `failed` is one the supervisor tried to revive and ran out of
attempts for. Nothing is running in its pane. A prompt into it is the same failure
as User Story 1 reached by a different road, and it gets the same answer.

**Why this priority**: it is the same host exposure, and it is one comparison.

**Independent Test**: POST a prompt to a session recorded `failed`; the answer is
`409` and the fake controller recorded no command at all.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** a session in state `failed`, **When** a prompt is posted, **Then**
   the answer is `409` `{"error":"session not ready"}` and no tmux command ran.
2. **Given** a session in state `dead`, **When** a prompt is posted, **Then** the
   answer is exactly what it is today — the resolver's uniform `404` — and this
   feature changes nothing about it.

---

### User Story 3 - A multi-line prompt arrives once, whole, as text (Priority: P1)

The opp-lease handoff sends a multi-line item body. Under a plain paste a harness
can submit line one early and treat the rest as a second turn. A bracketed paste
is the form both harnesses read as one block of text.

**Why this priority**: it is the correctness half of the requirement that the
route carries what the caller wrote, and lawnmower's real payloads are multi-line.

**Independent Test**: deliver a two-line prompt and assert one bracketed paste
followed by exactly one Enter — against the fake, and against a real tmux pane
running `cat`.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** a Claude session, **When** a two-line prompt is delivered, **Then**
   the controller recorded one `PasteBracketed` and one Enter, in that order, and
   no plain `Paste`.
2. **Given** a Codex session, **When** a prompt is delivered, **Then** it is also
   bracketed. `Prompt` no longer asks which harness it is talking to.
3. **Given** a compact, **When** it is delivered, **Then** it still uses the
   harness-based paste it uses today. Its payload is a daemon constant.
4. **Given** a prompt holding `ESC [ 2 0 1 ~`, **When** it is posted, **Then** it
   is refused with `400` and nothing reaches the pane (FR-007).

---

### User Story 4 - A prompt that is really a command is refused (Priority: P2)

A client that meant to say something and instead sent `/clear` discards the
conversation it was trying to continue; one that sent `!rm -rf …` runs a shell
command in the session's own unsandboxed context. On the API door those two
leading characters are a client bug, and the daemon can see it.

**Why this priority**: it is cheap, it is decided at the boundary, and no measured
caller is refused by it. It ranks below the three above because a client has to
send it deliberately.

**Independent Test**: POST `"/clear"`; the answer is `400` and the fake recorded
nothing. POST the same text through the browser type route; it is delivered.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** a prompt whose first non-whitespace character is `/` or `!`, **When**
   it is posted to the API door, **Then** the answer is `400` with the uniform
   bad-request body and no tmux command ran.
2. **Given** a prompt whose *later* line begins with `/`, **When** it is posted,
   **Then** it is delivered. The rule reads the first non-whitespace character of
   the whole text and nothing else.
3. **Given** the operator typing `/compact` into the session page's input panel,
   **When** they press Send, **Then** it is delivered unchanged. The browser door
   is not touched by this rule.

---

### User Story 5 - Two writers cannot interleave inside one pane (Priority: P2)

A prompt that arrives while a revive or a continue is typing a new command line
into the pane lands partly in the dying process and partly in the next one. The
session lock does not exclude a restart, because a restart does not hold it for
its whole run.

**Why this priority**: it is a real corruption, and it is rare — it needs a prompt
to arrive inside a restart's window.

**Independent Test**: hold the restart claim, POST a prompt, and see `409` with no
tmux command recorded.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** a revive or continue holding the session's restart claim, **When** a
   prompt is posted, **Then** the answer is `409` `{"error":"session not ready"}`
   and no tmux command ran. The prompt does not wait for the restart.
2. **Given** two prompts to one session at the same moment, **When** both run,
   **Then** each uses its own tmux buffer name and neither one's Enter lands
   between the other's paste and Enter.

---

### User Story 6 - A caller can find its own delivery in the trail (Priority: P3)

A client that delivered a prompt and then lost its answer — a timeout, a daemon
restart — has no way to tell whether the text landed. The audit trail is the only
durable record of a delivery, and today it carries nothing the caller chose.

**Why this priority**: it is an operability feature, not a safety one, and it is
the only requirement here that adds a field rather than a refusal.

**Independent Test**: POST with `"request_id":"abc-123"`; the `202` echoes it and
the audit record carries it. POST a 33-character or upper-case one; `400`.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** a body carrying a valid `request_id`, **When** the prompt is
   delivered, **Then** the `202` echoes the value and the request's one audit
   record carries it in a field named `request_id`.
2. **Given** a body carrying an invalid `request_id`, **When** it arrives,
   **Then** the answer is `400` and no tmux command ran.
3. **Given** a body carrying no `request_id`, **When** the prompt is delivered,
   **Then** the field appears nowhere — not in the response, not on the record.
   An existing client sees byte-for-byte the response it sees today.
4. **Given** a refused prompt that carried a valid `request_id`, **When** it is
   refused, **Then** the Deny record carries the same field.

---

### Edge Cases

- **A prompt holding `ESC [ 2 0 1 ~`.** Under today's plain paste the bytes are
  inert; under FR-005's bracketed paste they would end the paste early and the
  remainder would reach the pane as keystrokes. FR-007 refuses the payload, so it
  cannot arrive. This is the one exposure bracketing *creates*, and it is closed
  in the same change that creates it.
- **A prompt holding a bare `\r`.** Refused by FR-007 as a C0 control. This door
  does not CRLF-normalise the way the session page's route does: the API door's
  text is delivered byte-for-byte, and rewriting it here would deliver something
  the caller did not send. No measured caller sends one.
- **A prompt between 16 KiB and the body bound.** Delivered. FR-007 adopts the
  character rule and deliberately **not** the session page's 16384-byte bound; the
  prompt route keeps the body bound it has today.
- **A later line beginning `/` or `!`.** Delivered (FR-008). The `resume.txt`
  fixture holds a line beginning `/compact` for exactly this reason.
- **A pane that falls back to a shell between the second liveness read and the
  Enter.** Not covered, and not claimed to be: the window is two tmux commands
  wide and nothing measured it (research.md "Not verified").
- **A Codex composer meeting the `C-u` of FR-003.** `C-u` clears a Claude composer
  and a shell line; Codex's was not measured. The worst case is a composer left
  holding text that was never submitted, which is the state a refused prompt is
  supposed to leave behind.
- **A session parked on a dialog.** Still accepts a prompt. `parked_on` and
  `suspicious_dialog` keep reporting it in the `202` and keep not refusing — the
  readiness signal that would refuse it is out of scope (D8).
- **A `request_id` reused by the caller.** The daemon does not deduplicate. It is a
  correlation value the caller chose, not a key the daemon owns, and a route that
  remembered one would be keeping state about callers it deliberately keeps none
  about.

## Requirements *(mandatory)*

### Readiness

- **FR-001**: `Manager.Prompt` MUST read the session's row from the controller's
  `List` before any tmux command that changes anything, and branch on its `Claude`
  liveness: `LivenessStopped` refuses, `LivenessUnknown` and `LivenessRunning`
  deliver, and a `List` that fails is an error and never a delivery. It MUST NOT
  add a method to `tmuxctl.Controller`, so the `k8s/` module's `podctl` is
  untouched.
- **FR-002**: Readiness MUST NOT be decided by reading what the pane shows. Spec
  012 FR-007 forbids it for detection and pane content is secret under
  `docs/security.md` §3; `paneDialogState` stays what it is, additive information
  and never a gate.
- **FR-003**: `Manager.Prompt` MUST read liveness a second time after the paste and
  before the Enter. If that read is `LivenessStopped` it MUST send `C-u`, MUST NOT
  send Enter, and MUST refuse. No third read is required: the lost-Enter window
  measured by the probe is the first seconds after launch, which is out of scope.
- **FR-004**: `Manager.Prompt` MUST refuse a session in state `failed` before any
  tmux command. A session in state `dead` keeps today's answer unchanged.

### The refusal

- **FR-005**: `internal/session` MUST gain exactly one sentinel,
  `ErrSessionNotReady`, and every refusal FR-001, FR-003, FR-004 and FR-010 make
  MUST return it. `refusePrompt` MUST map it to `409` with body
  `{"error":"session not ready"}`, and the request's one audit record MUST be a
  Deny whose reason is the constant `session not ready`. That reason names no
  state, no pane content and no prompt. No other status, body or reason is added
  to this route.

### Delivery

- **FR-006**: `Manager.Prompt` MUST deliver with `PasteBracketed` for every
  harness — one paste, then at most one Enter. `Manager.Compact` MUST keep the
  harness-based paste it uses today; its payload is a daemon constant, not caller
  text. No rule refusing newlines may be added: the opp-lease handoff pastes
  multi-line bodies, and bracketing is what makes a newline safe.
- **FR-007**: Because FR-006 brackets this route's paste, the prompt text MUST be
  refused when it is not valid UTF-8, or holds any byte in `0x00–0x1F` other than
  `0x09` and `0x0A`, or holds `0x7F`. This is the rule `docs/security.md` §2
  already states for bracketed paste and `session.ValidateTyped` already applies
  for the session page (spec 018 FR-004), and it MUST be **the same predicate
  rather than a second copy** — two spellings of one rule are free to disagree,
  and the one that disagrees is the one nobody reads. The refusal MUST be `400`
  with the uniform bad-request body, before any tmux command.
  - The **length** half of `ValidateTyped` is deliberately not adopted. The prompt
    route keeps the bound it has today (`CRSW_MAX_BODY_BYTES`, default 65536);
    taking `MaxTypeBytes` (16384) with it would tighten a live route's bound for
    no requirement, which is a client break wearing a safety check's clothes.
  - This door MUST NOT CRLF-normalise. The session page's route rewrites `\r\n`
    before validating because a textarea produces it; the API door delivers caller
    bytes unaltered, so a `\r` is refused rather than rewritten.
- **FR-008**: The API door MUST refuse a prompt whose first character that is not
  space, tab, CR or LF is `!` or `/`, with `400` and the uniform bad-request body,
  before any tmux command. The rule reads the first non-whitespace character of
  the whole text and no other character. The session page's type route MUST be
  unchanged, and a test MUST assert that it still delivers `/compact`.

### Concurrency

- **FR-009**: `Manager.Prompt` MUST take the restart claim (`claimRestart`,
  non-blocking) **after** `lockSession`, and MUST release it on return. The order
  matches `Continue`'s, so no new lock ordering enters the package.
- **FR-010**: A prompt that finds the restart claim held MUST refuse with
  `ErrSessionNotReady` and MUST run no tmux command. It MUST NOT wait: a prompt
  that blocked across a process restart would hold the request open, and a caller
  cannot tell a slow delivery from a lost one.
- **FR-011**: The two guarantees already true MUST be asserted rather than assumed
  — the per-session mutex is held across the paste and the Enter together, and
  each paste draws its own tmux buffer name. A test MUST show two concurrent
  prompts using distinct buffer names and never interleaving a paste and a submit.

### Correlation

- **FR-012**: `promptRequest` MUST gain one optional field, `request_id`, of 1 to
  32 characters drawn from `[a-z0-9-]`. A value outside that is a `400` decided at
  the boundary, before any tmux command. The body stays decoded with
  `DisallowUnknownFields`, so no other new field is accepted.
- **FR-013**: A valid `request_id` MUST be echoed in the `202` body and written to
  the request's one audit record under the key `request_id`. An absent one MUST
  appear nowhere: the field is omitted from the response and from the record, so a
  client that sends none sees today's bytes.
- **FR-014**: The record MUST gain the `request_id` and **nothing about the
  prompt** — not its text, not its length, not a hash of it. `Record.Reason` stays
  server-authored sentinels and MUST NOT carry the value; `request_id` is the one
  field on the record whose bytes a caller chose.

### Bounds on the change

- **FR-015**: The API door MUST still have exactly six routes, and this feature
  MUST NOT add a package under `internal/`, a dependency, a `go.sum`, or a
  `tmuxctl.Controller` method.
- **FR-016**: Every payload shape ai-lawnmower sends today — board answer, requeue
  resume, opp-lease batch handoff, opp-lease follow-up — MUST still answer `202`
  with `"delivered":true`. The four are fixed byte-for-byte as test fixtures so
  that a later change to any rule here is measured against the traffic rather than
  argued about.
- **FR-017**: `docs/security.md` MUST gain a "Prompt route gates (spec 020)"
  subsection under "Non-negotiables", naming the liveness gate, the `failed`
  refusal, the bracketed paste and the control-character rule it brings, the
  leading-character rule, the restart claim and `request_id`. `AGENTS.md` MUST NOT
  be edited, and MUST stay under the 150-line CI limit.

### Amendments to shipped specifications

- **FR-018**: Spec 018 **FR-006** ("the API door's `POST /sessions/{id}/prompt`
  MUST be unchanged: plain paste, then Enter. Bracketed paste is for the
  interactive route only") is amended by FR-006, FR-007 and FR-008 of this
  specification: the route's paste becomes bracketed, it gains the
  control-character rule that bracketing makes load-bearing, and it gains one
  refusal the interactive route does not have. Nothing else about the interactive
  route changes, and spec 018's own FR-004 is untouched.
- **FR-019**: Spec 001 **FR-042** (an audit record carries no prompt text, no
  session output, no credential and no shared secret) is amended for exactly one
  field by FR-013 and FR-014: the record may carry a caller-supplied `request_id`
  of at most 32 characters from `[a-z0-9-]`. Everything else FR-042 forbids stays
  forbidden, and the alphabet is what keeps the field from becoming a channel for
  the text — 32 bytes of that set cannot carry a prompt.

### Out of scope

- **FR-020**: A readiness gate reading Claude Code's session registry
  (`sessions/<pid>.json`) is **not** built here. It was stated as a MAY; probe
  check 8 left open whether the daemon can read that file at all under spec 017's
  v2 option B, so a gate built on it would work on the VM and be blind in the
  cluster; and probe checks 3 and 9 show the registry misses the trust dialog and
  a half-typed draft, so it answers "a session exists" rather than "this session
  will read what I send next". Deferring a MAY is a decision, and research.md D8
  records it as one. The cost is stated there: a session parked on a dialog still
  accepts a prompt.
- **FR-021**: Also out of scope, each with its reason in research.md D9: opening a
  Claude transcript or registry file from Go (spec 013 FR-025 is unchanged);
  holding or calling an LLM; a seventh API route; free text on the browser door
  beyond spec 018; the startup lost-Enter window (probe check 1b); and the socket
  transport, which belongs to the lm-steer-write milestone.

**Key Entities**: **Liveness**, the existing three-valued `tmuxctl` answer derived
from `@crswd-binary` against the pane's current command — running, stopped,
unknown. **Not-ready**, one condition with one sentinel and one answer, covering a
stopped pane, a `failed` session and a held restart claim; the caller cannot tell
the three apart because to a caller they are one event, *not now, try later*.
**`request_id`**, a caller-chosen correlation value, bounded in length and
alphabet, and the only caller bytes on an audit record.

## Success Criteria *(mandatory)*

- **SC-001**: `go test ./internal/... -run Prompt` proves, against the fake
  controller, each of: a stopped pane answers `409` `{"error":"session not ready"}`
  with no paste; a `failed` session the same with no tmux command at all; an exit
  between the paste and the Enter yields `C-u`, no Enter and `409`; a held restart
  claim yields `409` with no tmux command.
- **SC-002**: `go test -tags tmux ./internal/session/ -run Prompt` proves on a real
  tmux that a pane on `sh` carrying `@crswd-binary` `claude` is refused and reads
  back empty, and that a two-line prompt into `cat` arrives once.
- **SC-003**: `go test ./internal/httpapi/ -run 'Prompt|Type'` proves that a
  leading `/` or `!` answers `400` with nothing delivered, and that the session
  page's type route still delivers `/compact`.
- **SC-004**: `go test ./internal/httpapi/ -run RequestID` proves that a valid
  `request_id` is echoed and audited, that a 33-character or upper-case one answers
  `400` with nothing delivered, and that an absent one appears nowhere.
- **SC-005**: `go test ./internal/httpapi/ -run Lawnmower` posts all four fixtures
  and gets `202` `"delivered":true` for each.
- **SC-006**: The leak suite finds no prompt text, no length and no hash of it in
  any audit record or log line, with the new field present.
- **SC-007**: `grep -cE '^## \`(GET|POST|DELETE|PATCH|PUT) '
  specs/001-crswd-daemon-core/contracts/http-api.md` prints `6`, and a diff of
  `internal/`'s directories against `main` is empty.
- **SC-008**: `go test ./...`, `go test -tags tmux ./...`,
  `go vet -tags quickstart ./cmd/crswd` and `golangci-lint run` all exit 0, and
  `go.sum` still does not exist.

## Assumptions

- `@crswd-binary` against the pane's current command is a true liveness signal for
  the sessions this route serves. Probe check 13 measured 6 of 6 live panes,
  three of them `rcq`.
- ai-lawnmower is the only client of this route. The grep that found no caller
  refused by FR-008 covered that client; an unknown client sending a leading `/`,
  a control byte or a bare `\r` is refused with a `400` it can see and fix.
- `409 {"error":"session not ready"}` needs no client change: lawnmower's
  `deliver()` already treats any body carrying an `error` key as a refusal.
- A refusal is cheaper than a wrong delivery on this route, because a wrong
  delivery is a command line in an unsandboxed shell and a refusal is a retry.

3	**Branch**: `plan/interactive-input` | **Date**: 2026-10-06 | **Spec**: [spec.md](spec.md)
4	
5	## Summary
6	
7	The session page gains three things under the pane:
8	
9	- a textarea that delivers the operator's text by bracketed paste, optionally
10	  followed by Enter;
11	- a key bar that sends one of twelve allowlisted keys;
12	- a closed Scrollback disclosure that fetches up to 5000 lines of tmux history
13	  when opened.
14	
15	Underneath, `tmuxctl` gains `PasteBracketed` and `CaptureHistory`, and every
16	session is created with `history-limit 5000`. `session` gains `Type`, `PressKey`
17	and `History`. `httpapi` gains two `handleAction` routes, one `handleBrowser`
18	GET, one rate bucket and three audit actions. Nothing here is specific to
19	Claude Code, so spec 019 inherits it for Codex unchanged.
20	
21	## Technical Context
22	
23	**Language**: Go stdlib only, server-rendered templates, one hand-written
24	`crswd.js`. **Storage**: none. **Testing**: table-driven, `t.Parallel()`, the
25	tmux fake for everything except the three `-tags tmux` cases in
26	`internal/tmuxctl/exec_tmux_test.go`, which need a real tmux. **Measured inputs**:
27	research.md R1 (bracketed paste), R2 (history-limit), R3 (key bytes).

29	## Constitution Check
30	
31	| Principle | Assessment | Pass |
32	|---|---|---|
33	| **I — Security is a gate** | Both writes go through `handleAction`: identity, `Sec-Fetch-Site` with absent refused, page token, body cap. The ownership check uses `View`. Caller text travels on stdin only. Keys come from a closed map to daemon constants. Control bytes are refused, so a typed payload cannot close the bracketed paste. The history GET refuses cross-site as the stream does. The audit records the action and never the text, key or history. | ✅ |
34	| **II — Unknowns surfaced** | The two questions code cannot answer, the phone-only ones, ship UNANSWERED with fallbacks (FR-021). The two behaviours that could have been guessed, multi-line paste and history-limit timing, were measured first. | ✅ |
35	| **III — Verifiable** | Every FR is a status code, an argv, a byte sequence on a real tmux, a template string, or an audit record a test reads. | ✅ |
36	| **IV — Smallest change** | Reuses the token bucket, the action gate, the outcome banner, `Strip`, `.pane`, `.button` and `.field-input`. `Paste` and `/prompt` are untouched (research R1). | ✅ |
37	| **V — Standards enforced** | The leak suite, the refusal-shape sweep and the stylesheet sweeps gain the new routes and classes instead of being relaxed. | ✅ |

39	| **VII — Design system** | Five new classes, all built from existing tokens. No new breakpoint, no inline style, no new font size. The pane's text-only rendering is unchanged. | ✅ |

# Implementation Plan: Interactive Input on the Session Page

**Branch**: `plan/interactive-input` | **Date**: 2026-10-06 | **Spec**: [spec.md](spec.md)

## Summary

The session page gains three things under the pane:

- a textarea that delivers the operator's text by bracketed paste, optionally
  followed by Enter;
- a key bar that sends one of twelve allowlisted keys;
- a closed Scrollback disclosure that fetches up to 5000 lines of tmux history
  when opened.

Underneath, `tmuxctl` gains `PasteBracketed` and `CaptureHistory`, and every
session is created with `history-limit 5000`. `session` gains `Type`, `PressKey`
and `History`. `httpapi` gains two `handleAction` routes, one `handleBrowser`
GET, one rate bucket and three audit actions. Nothing here is specific to
Claude Code, so spec 019 inherits it for Codex unchanged.

## Technical Context

**Language**: Go stdlib only, server-rendered templates, one hand-written
`crswd.js`. **Storage**: none. **Testing**: table-driven, `t.Parallel()`, the
tmux fake for everything except the three `-tags tmux` cases in
`internal/tmuxctl/exec_tmux_test.go`, which need a real tmux. **Measured inputs**:
research.md R1 (bracketed paste), R2 (history-limit), R3 (key bytes).

## Constitution Check

| Principle | Assessment | Pass |
|---|---|---|
| **I — Security is a gate** | Both writes go through `handleAction`: identity, `Sec-Fetch-Site` with absent refused, page token, body cap. The ownership check uses `View`. Caller text travels on stdin only. Keys come from a closed map to daemon constants. Control bytes are refused, so a typed payload cannot close the bracketed paste. The history GET refuses cross-site as the stream does. The audit records the action and never the text, key or history. | ✅ |
| **II — Unknowns surfaced** | The two questions code cannot answer, the phone-only ones, ship UNANSWERED with fallbacks (FR-021). The two behaviours that could have been guessed, multi-line paste and history-limit timing, were measured first. | ✅ |
| **III — Verifiable** | Every FR is a status code, an argv, a byte sequence on a real tmux, a template string, or an audit record a test reads. | ✅ |
| **IV — Smallest change** | Reuses the token bucket, the action gate, the outcome banner, `Strip`, `.pane`, `.button` and `.field-input`. `Paste` and `/prompt` are untouched (research R1). | ✅ |
| **V — Standards enforced** | The leak suite, the refusal-shape sweep and the stylesheet sweeps gain the new routes and classes instead of being relaxed. | ✅ |
| **VI — Blast radius** | Bounds are constants: 16384 bytes of text, 240/min, 5000 history lines, 4 MiB of history. No caller value reaches an argv. The rule amendment (FR-001) narrows the exception to an operator pressing a control. | ✅ |
| **VII — Design system** | Five new classes, all built from existing tokens. No new breakpoint, no inline style, no new font size. The pane's text-only rendering is unchanged. | ✅ |

## Project Structure

```text
internal/tmuxctl/
├── controller.go        MOD  PasteBracketed, CaptureHistory on the interface; HistoryLimit
├── fake.go              MOD  argvNew chain; argvPasteBufferBracketed; argvCaptureHistory;
│                             OpPasteBracketed, OpCaptureHistory; Fake methods; SetHistory
├── exec.go              MOD  Exec.PasteBracketed, Exec.CaptureHistory, ErrHistoryTooLarge
├── argv.go              MOD  ArgvPasteBracketed, ArgvCaptureHistory wrappers
├── argv_test.go         MOD  wrapper equality rows
├── fake_test.go         MOD  new-session argv row; new method rows
├── exec_test.go         MOD  new-session argv row; new method rows
└── exec_tmux_test.go    MOD  three real-tmux cases
internal/session/
├── input.go             NEW  Key, ParseKey, Keys, MaxTypeBytes, ValidateTyped, Type, PressKey, History
├── input_test.go        NEW
└── manager_test.go      MOD  new-session argv row (line 219)
internal/httpapi/
├── input.go             NEW  three routes, fields, sentinels
├── input_test.go        NEW
├── outcome.go           MOD  six outcome codes + sentences
├── server.go            MOD  inputs limiter; three registrations
├── dashboard_test.go    MOD  pane-note assertion keeps passing (no edit expected); input panel render test
└── stylesheet_test.go   MOD  script sweeps for the input client
internal/audit/
├── audit.go             MOD  ActionDashboardType, ActionDashboardKey, ActionDashboardHistory
├── audit_test.go        MOD  both action tables
└── leak_test.go         MOD  drive dashboard.type with a canary
web/templates/partials/pane.html   MOD  note copy; input panel; key bar; scrollback
web/static/crswd.css                MOD  .input-panel .type-form .key-bar .scrollback .scrollback-summary
web/static/crswd.js                 MOD  input client; shared handler skips data-session-input
cmd/crswd/quickstart_dashboard_test.go  MOD  only if the note assertion breaks (it should not: FR-020 keeps the phrase)
specs/001-crswd-daemon-core/contracts/tmuxctl.md  MOD  new-session chain; two new commands
AGENTS.md, docs/security.md, docs/components.md, docs/mobile-open-questions.md  MOD
```

## Cross-spec notes

- **Spec 017 (kubernetes)**: its second `tmuxctl.Controller` (`internal/podctl`,
  not yet on main) must implement `PasteBracketed` and `CaptureHistory` using
  `ArgvPasteBracketed` and `ArgvCaptureHistory`. `ArgvNew` already carries the
  history-limit chain, so the pod gets it for free. Record this in spec 017's
  next plan revision. It is not edited here.
- **Spec 019 (Codex)**: start Codex with `--no-alt-screen`, or tmux keeps no
  history for it (research R1 table, `alternate_on=0` measured). Codex can also
  open on an update prompt and a "Hooks need review" prompt (seen during the
