1	# Research: prompt route safety
2	
3	**Spec**: [spec.md](spec.md) · **Plan**: [plan.md](plan.md) · **Tasks**: [tasks.md](tasks.md)
4	
5	This feature hardens `POST /sessions/{id}/prompt`, the one API route that already
6	delivers free text into a running session. It is the route ai-lawnmower's `answer`
7	and opp-lease handoff call today, so every change here is a change to a live client.
8	
9	## Where the evidence comes from
10	
11	Three sources, and each decision below says which one it leans on.
12	
13	| Tag | Source | Status |
14	|---|---|---|
15	| **Probe** | `~/code/ai-lawnmower/ralph/plans/lm-steer-design/results.md`, numbered checks | Outside this repo, read-only. The checks this feature turns on are transcribed into `ralph/plans/lm-steer-crswd-018/PROGRESS.md` ("Probe results that decide this plan") because the loop that implements this spec cannot reach that path |
16	| **Design** | `~/code/ai-lawnmower/docs/mcp-session-steering-design.md`, section (g) "Phase 3 detail" | Outside this repo, read-only. It is where requirements 1 to 7 are stated |
17	| **Code** | This repository at `30941f3` | Read and re-read in tree on 10/14/26; the line references below were checked, not remembered |
18	
19	The decisions were taken during planning, before any task ran, and are recorded in
20	`ralph/plans/lm-steer-crswd-018/IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md` under "Decisions already
21	made". They are reproduced here with their evidence. **They are not reopened by the
22	implementation**; a task that finds one of them wrong stops and says so rather than
23	choosing differently.
24	
25	## The route as it stands (Code, 10/14/26)
26	
27	What the hardening is measured against:
28	
29	- `internal/httpapi/sessions.go` `promptSession` (line 772) decodes `promptRequest`,
30	  best-effort-reads the pane for a known dialog (`paneDialogState`, which is
31	  additive information and never a gate), calls `Manager.Prompt`, and answers `202`
32	  with `{"id","delivered","parked_on","suspicious_dialog"}`.
33	- `refusePrompt` (line 849) maps `session.ErrEmptyPrompt` to `400` and **everything
34	  else to a `500` with no detail**. There is no 409 on this route today.
35	- `internal/session/manager.go` `Manager.Prompt` (line 1194) refuses an empty ID
36	  (`ErrSessionNotFound`), `StateDead` (`ErrSessionDead`) and empty text
37	  (`ErrEmptyPrompt`); takes `lockSession`; calls `m.paste`; then `SendKeys` Enter.
38	- `m.paste` (line 1253) is bracketed **only** when the harness spec says
39	  `BracketedPaste`, which Claude's does not (spec 019 D9 left that to spec 018, and
40	  spec 018 FR-006 declined it for the API door).
41	- `Manager.Prompt` does **not** read liveness, does **not** consult `StateFailed`,
42	  and does **not** take the restart claim.
43	
44	So a prompt into a session whose Claude has exited lands in a login shell as a
45	command line, and a prompt racing a revival lands half in one process and half in
46	the next. Those are the two failures this feature closes.
47	
48	---
49	
50	## D1 Spec number
51	
52	**Decision.** This feature is `specs/020-prompt-route-safety/`.
53	
54	**Evidence.** The design calls it "crswd spec 018", but `specs/018-interactive-input`
55	(the session page's input panel) and `specs/019-codex-runtime` already exist in this
56	repository (Code: `ls specs/`). 020 is the first free number.
57	
58	The milestone directory keeps the design's name — `ralph/plans/lm-steer-crswd-018/` —
59	because the lawnmower side refers to it that way. The mismatch is deliberate and is
60	stated in `VALIDATION_CONTRACT.md` so that a later reader does not "fix" one to match
61	the other.
62	
63	---
64	
65	## D2 Liveness gate (requirement 1)
66	
67	**Decision.** `Manager.Prompt` reads the session's row from the controller's `List`
68	and branches on its `Claude` liveness:
69	
70	- `LivenessStopped` → refuse with `ErrSessionNotReady`, before any tmux command that
71	  changes anything.
72	- `LivenessUnknown` → deliver.
73	- `LivenessRunning` → deliver.
74	- A `List` that fails → an error, not a delivery.
75	
76	The gate runs **twice**: once before the paste, and again after the paste and before
77	the Enter. If the second read is stopped, the daemon sends `C-u` and no Enter.
78	
79	**Evidence.**
80	
81	- Probe check 13: `@crswd-binary` matched `pane_current_command` on 6 of 6 live panes,
82	  three of them `rcq` panes. So the option the daemon already sets is a true liveness
83	  signal for the sessions lawnmower actually drives, not only for the plain case.
84	- Code: `tmuxctl.SessionInfo.Claude` is the three-valued `Liveness`
85	  (`internal/tmuxctl/controller.go:312-341`), derived from `@crswd-binary` against the
86	  pane's current command — by one tmux format in `Exec` (`exec.go:548`) and by
87	  `livenessOf` in the fake (`fake.go:251`). Both exist already; nothing new is
88	  measured here.
89	- Spec 012 FR-006 ("detect a session whose Claude process has stopped while its shell
90	  survives") is the requirement this reads, and `supervisor.go:153-156` already treats
91	  `LivenessUnknown` as healthy with a comment saying it must. This gate reads it the
92	  same way, so a session created before `@crswd-binary` existed keeps working.
93	- Probe check 1: there is no check-then-Enter race after the first turn; the lost-Enter
94	  window is the first ~5 s after launch, which is out of scope (D9). That is why two
95	  reads around the paste are enough and a third is not.
96	
97	**Why `List` and not a new method.** A per-session liveness method on
98	`tmuxctl.Controller` would force a matching change in the k8s module's `podctl`
99	(Code: `k8s/` is a second module reaching the root's `internal/` through `replace ../`).
100	This milestone adds no `Controller` method, so `podctl` is untouched and the cluster
101	build does not move.
102	
103	**Why the second read, and why `C-u`.** Between the paste and the Enter the pane can
104	fall back to a shell — Claude exits, the composer's text is gone, and the Enter would
105	submit whatever the paste left on the shell's line as a command. `C-u` clears that
106	line; sending no Enter means nothing runs. Refusing *after* a paste is not as good as
107	refusing before one, and the `C-u` is what makes the imperfect case harmless rather
108	than merely reported.
109	
110	*Rejected: refusing `LivenessUnknown`.* It is the state of every session started by a
111	build older than the option, and refusing it would make this route stop working for
112	sessions the supervisor itself calls healthy — two answers to one question.
113	
114	*Rejected: reading the pane's text to decide readiness.* Spec 012 FR-007 forbids it
115	for detection, pane content is secret under `docs/security.md` §3, and `paneDialogState`
116	already shows what a text read is good for: additive information, never a gate.
117	
118	---
119	
120	## D3 Not-ready answer (requirements 1, 2 and 5)
121	
122	**Decision.** One new sentinel, `session.ErrSessionNotReady`. Every refusal this
123	feature adds inside `internal/session` returns it, and `refusePrompt` maps it to
124	`409` with body `{"error":"session not ready"}` and an audit **Deny** whose reason is
125	the constant `session not ready`.
126	
127	A session in `StateFailed` gets it. `StateDead` keeps today's answer unchanged.
128	
129	**Evidence.**
130	
131	- Code: `StateFailed` (`internal/session/session.go:86`) means the supervisor tried to
132	  bring the session back and ran out of attempts (`supervisor.go:311-314`). Nothing is
133	  running in that pane, so a prompt into it is the same failure as a stopped pane;
134	  `Manager.Prompt` refuses `StateDead` today and says nothing about `StateFailed`.
135	- Code: a dead session is already refused as a `404` by the resolver before
136	  `promptSession` runs, and `refusePrompt`'s comment says reaching its `ErrSessionDead`
137	  branch would mean a record went terminal between two layers of one request. Leaving
138	  `dead` alone keeps that path exactly as it is and keeps the enumeration rule
139	  (`docs/security.md`: a session the caller may not have is a 404, never a 403/409).
140	- lawnmower's `deliver()` (`~/code/ai-lawnmower/loop/session_resume.py`, as recorded in
141	  PROGRESS.md on 10/14/26) treats **any** body carrying an `error` key as a refusal. So
142	  `409 {"error":"session not ready"}` reads as a refusal to the existing client with no
143	  client change, which is why the body carries `error` and not a new key.
144	- `docs/security.md` "Rate limiting & audit": every reason on the trail is a sentinel
145	  this codebase authored. `session not ready` is one. It names no state, no pane
146	  content and no prompt — an operator reading the trail learns that the route refused
147	  and why in the daemon's own words, and a caller learns nothing about the host it
148	  could not already see.
149	
150	*Rejected: a sentinel per reason* (stopped pane, failed state, restart held). Three
151	sentinels reaching one status code with one body is three things to keep in step for
152	a distinction the caller cannot observe. The trail distinguishes nothing more here
153	because the three are the same event to the client: not now, try later.
154	
155	*Rejected: `503`.* The condition is about one named session, not about this daemon's
156	capacity, and `409` is already the contract's "the host's state refuses this" code
157	(the unverified-teardown answer, `sessions.go:749`).
158	
159	---
160	
161	## D4 Bracketed paste (requirement 3)
162	
163	**Decision.** `Manager.Prompt` pastes with `PasteBracketed` for **every** harness.
164	`Manager.Compact` keeps its harness-based paste (`m.paste`). No newline refusal.
165	
166	**Evidence.**
167	
168	- Code: `Controller.PasteBracketed` already exists (spec 018 added it; `paste-buffer -p`,
169	  `internal/tmuxctl/exec.go:220-230`), and the session page's type route already uses it
170	  for every harness. This decision reuses that method; it adds none.
171	- `docs/security.md` §2: inside a bracketed paste the terminal does not interpret the
172	  pasted bytes, which is what makes multi-line text one paste instead of a line of text
173	  plus a submit plus another line. The same section already requires that caller text
174	  reach tmux only through `load-buffer` on stdin and then `paste-buffer`, bracketed on
175	  the session page's route; this extends the bracketing to the API door's route.
176	- Spec 019 D9 / research M3–M5 measured that Codex swallows the Enter after a *plain*
177	  paste and submits correctly after a bracketed one. Claude accepts both. So bracketed
178	  is the one form that is correct for both harnesses, and `Prompt` stops needing to ask
179	  which harness it is talking to at all.
180	**A consequence this decision does not close, named rather than smoothed over.**
181	`docs/security.md` §2 says text holding a C0 control other than TAB or LF is refused,
182	"because inside a bracketed paste `ESC[201~` would end the paste" — and that sentence
183	is about **the session page's route**. The refusal is `session.ValidateTyped`
184	(`internal/session/input.go:75-92`, spec 018 FR-004), and Code confirms it is called by
185	`Manager.Type` (`input.go:105`) and **not** by `Manager.Prompt`: the API door's
186	`promptRequest.Text` is validated only for emptiness and the body-size bound
187	(`internal/httpapi/sessions.go:264-270`, "that is the whole of its validation
188	(FR-030)"). So bracketing this route's paste makes a byte sequence relevant that was
189	inert under a plain paste: a caller that sent `\x1b[201~` mid-text would end the paste
190	early and the remainder would reach the pane as keystrokes rather than as pasted text.
191	
192	D4 as decided adds no refusal, so this feature does not close it, and this document
193	does not invent one. What is recorded here is that the mechanism already exists
194	(`ValidateTyped`, one call away) and that spec.md has to say which way it goes —
195	either the route gains that check or the exposure is accepted in writing. It is logged
196	as a finding in `ralph/plans/lm-steer-crswd-018/PROGRESS.md` so the task that writes
197	spec.md cannot miss it. No measured client sends a control byte: every fixture in
198	PROGRESS.md "Payload fixtures" is printable text plus newlines.
199	
200	**Why no newline refusal.** The opp-lease handoff pastes multi-line item bodies
201	(Probe/Design: the builders in `console.py` and `lawnmower-route`, whose shapes are
202	fixed byte-for-byte as T011's fixtures in PROGRESS.md "Payload fixtures"). A rule
203	refusing `\n` would refuse the traffic this route exists to carry. Bracketing is what
204	makes a newline safe; refusing newlines would be the same protection obtained by
205	breaking the client.
206	
207	**Why `Compact` is untouched.** Its payload is a daemon constant, not caller text, and
208	spec 018 FR-006's "unchanged" promise about this route is amended here only for what
209	requirements 1 to 6 name. Changing `Compact` as well would be an unrequested change to
210	a path with no requirement behind it (constitution IV).
211	
212	This amends spec 018 **FR-006**, which says the API door's prompt route must be
213	unchanged — plain paste, then Enter, with bracketed paste reserved for the interactive
214	route. The amendment is recorded in spec.md, not left to this file.
215	
216	---
217	
218	## D5 Leading `!` or `/` (requirement 4)
219	
220	**Decision.** On the **API door only**: refuse a prompt whose first character that is
221	not space, tab, CR or LF is `!` or `/`. The answer is `400` with the uniform
222	bad-request body, decided before any tmux command runs. The session page's type route
223	is unchanged.
224	
225	**Evidence.**
226	
227	- Design, requirement 4: those two characters are Claude Code's slash-command and
228	  shell-escape prefixes. A prompt that begins with one is not a prompt — `/clear`
229	  discards the conversation the caller was trying to continue, and `!` runs a shell
230	  command in the session's own unsandboxed context. A client that meant to say
231	  something and instead silently reset the session is the failure being closed.
232	- Code grep of 10/14/26 over every lawnmower caller of this route: `console.py`
233	  `_answer_action` (via `session_resume.deliver`), `lawnmower-route` `resume_prompt`,
234	  `_batch_listing_prompt`, and `opp_followup_prompt` all build text whose first
235	  character is a letter. **No existing caller is refused by this rule.** That is the
236	  whole of why it can be added to a live route at all.
237	- The fixtures in PROGRESS.md keep the shape that matters: `resume.txt` holds a *later*
238	  line beginning `/compact`. The rule is about the first non-whitespace character of
239	  the whole text and nothing else, so that fixture is accepted. A rule scanning every
240	  line would refuse real traffic.
241	- The browser door is excluded because its route is the operator typing at their own
242	  session: `docs/security.md` records the session page's input panel as text or a key
243	  the operator sent, delivered once, when they pressed it. An operator typing
244	  `/compact` into their own session is the feature, not a mistake, and T004 asserts
245	  that it still arrives.
246	
247	*Rejected: stripping or escaping the leading character.* It would deliver something
248	the caller did not write, into a session that executes code. A refusal the client can
249	see and fix is strictly better than a silent rewrite.
250	
251	*Rejected: an allowlist of safe slash commands.* The daemon would then own a list that
252	tracks Claude Code's command set, and a stale list is a command delivered because
253	nobody updated a table. The route carries prompts; a caller that wants a command has
254	the browser door and the operator behind it.
255	
256	This amends spec 018 **FR-006** a second time (see D4): the route gains one refusal
257	the interactive route does not have.
258	
259	---
260	
261	## D6 Lock and buffer (requirement 5)
262	
263	**Decision.** `Manager.Prompt` takes the restart claim (`claimRestart`, non-blocking)
264	**after** `lockSession`, refuses with `ErrSessionNotReady` when a revive or a continue
265	already holds it, and releases it on return.
266	
267	**Evidence.**
268	
269	- Code: `lockSession` (`internal/session/input.go`) is already the per-session mutex
270	  shared by Type, PressKey, Prompt, Compact, SetMode, Continue, Destroy and the
271	  supervisor's Codex discovery. `Prompt` already takes it (`manager.go:1209`), so two
272	  concurrent prompts already cannot interleave paste and Enter.
273	- Code: `Exec.paste` already draws a fresh buffer name per paste (`newBufferName`,
274	  `exec.go:186-195`, 16 random hex digits behind `BufferPrefix`, "per call rather than
275	  per session, so a second paste into the same session cannot overwrite the first
276	  one's text before it lands"). The fake records the names through `nextBuffer`, so a
277	  test can assert they differ. Both halves of requirement 5's "distinct buffers, no
278	  interleaving" are therefore **already true**, from the spec 018 and 019 review
279	  passes, and this feature only has to prove it (T010) rather than build it.
280	- Code: `claimRestart` / `releaseRestart` (`manager.go:2674-2688`) are non-blocking and
281	  are what revival and continue hold while they type a new command line into the pane.
282	  That is the one concurrent writer `lockSession` does **not** exclude, because a
283	  restart does not hold the session lock for its whole run. A prompt pasted into a pane
284	  mid-restart lands partly in the dying process and partly on the shell the new command
285	  line is about to be typed at.
286	
287	**Why non-blocking.** A prompt that waited for a revival would hold an HTTP request
288	open across a process restart, and the caller cannot tell a slow delivery from a lost
289	one. `409 session not ready` is a fact the client can act on now; lawnmower's
290	`deliver()` already reads it as a refusal (D3).
291	
292	**Why after `lockSession` and not before.** The two are taken in one order everywhere
293	or they deadlock. `lockSession` first matches `Continue`'s order, so no new ordering
294	rule enters the package.
295	
296	---
297	
298	## D7 `request_id` (requirement 6)
299	
300	**Decision.** The prompt body gains one optional field, `request_id`: 1 to 32
301	characters of `[a-z0-9-]`. A value outside that is a `400`. A valid value is echoed in
302	the `202` body and written as `request_id` on the request's one audit record. Absent
303	means the field appears nowhere — not in the response, not on the record.
304	
305	**Evidence.**
306	
307	- Design, requirement 6: the caller needs to correlate a delivery it made with the
308	  record of that delivery, across a daemon restart and without a transcript. The audit
309	  trail is the only durable record of a prompt, and today it carries nothing the caller
310	  chose.
311	- Code: `audit.Record` (`internal/audit/audit.go:390-414`) has Action, Caller,
312	  SessionID, Decision, Reason and Remote. `RequestAudit`
313	  (`internal/httpapi/middleware.go`) has `SetSessionID` and `Deny`, so the
314	  carry-it-onto-the-one-record mechanism exists and gains one setter (T002) rather
315	  than a second record.
316	- The value goes in a **field of its own** and never into `Reason`. `Record.Reason`'s
317	  own documentation forbids caller-supplied text in it ("must never be built from
318	  caller-supplied text, a prompt, pane output, a token, or the shared secret"), and
319	  that rule is unamended: `Reason` stays server-authored sentinels, and `request_id`
320	  is the one field on the record whose bytes the caller chose.
321	- `docs/security.md` §2 and the decoder it shows: the body is decoded into a typed
322	  struct with `DisallowUnknownFields`, so the field has to be declared to be accepted
323	  at all, and anything else in the body is still refused.
324	
325	**Why that alphabet and that length.** The field is written to an audit record that an
326	operator reads and a tool greps. Lower-case, digits and `-` is the same shape this
327	repository already holds session names to (`^[a-zA-Z0-9-]{1,64}$`, `docs/security.md`
328	§2), minus the upper case; 32 characters fits a ULID or a UUID and leaves nothing for
329	a caller to smuggle. Validation is at the boundary and the refusal is a `400`, so no
330	tmux command runs for a body that was never going to be accepted.
331	
332	**Why this is not a hole in FR-042.** Spec 001 FR-042 forbids prompt text, session
333	output, credentials and the shared secret on an audit record, and nothing in it
334	contemplated a caller-chosen correlation value. This amends FR-042 for **this one
335	field**, and the bound is exact: the record gains the `request_id` the caller sent and
336	**nothing about the prompt** — not its text, not its length, not a hash of it. The
337	alphabet is what keeps the field from becoming a channel for the text itself: 32 bytes
338	of `[a-z0-9-]` cannot carry a prompt, and a caller that tried would be writing a value
339	an operator can see is not an identifier. The amendment is recorded in spec.md.
340	
341	---
342	
343	## D8 Registry gate (requirement 7) — deferred, not a clarification
344	
345	**Decision.** Requirement 7, a readiness gate reading Claude Code's session registry,
346	is **out of scope** for this feature. It is listed under Out of scope in spec.md with
347	this reason. It is **not** an open question in constitution II's sense — a deferred
348	MAY is a decision, and the marker that principle calls for is deliberately absent
349	from this directory. (Spelling that marker out here would also trip the gate that
350	greps this directory for it, which is why no file under `specs/020-prompt-route-safety/`
351	contains the phrase.)
352	
353	**Evidence.**
354	
355	- The design states requirement 7 as a **MAY**, not a MUST. Deferring a MAY is a scope
356	  decision, not an unanswered question, and constitution II is about requirements that
357	  are *ambiguous* — this one is clear and declined.
358	- Probe check 8 left open whether crswd can read `sessions/<pid>.json` at all under
359	  spec 017's v2 option B. No FR in spec 017 places that file in a pod, so a gate built
360	  on it would work on the VM and silently do nothing in the cluster — a readiness check
361	  that is right about one deployment and blind in the other.
362	- Probe checks 3 and 9: the registry misses the trust dialog and misses a half-typed
363	  draft in the composer. So it answers "a session exists" and not "this session will
364	  read what I send next", which is the question requirement 7 was asked to answer.
365	- The liveness gate (D2) is the part of requirement 1 that is measurable with what the
366	  daemon already holds, and it is what ships.
367	
368	**What this costs, stated rather than smoothed over.** A session sitting on a dialog
369	still accepts a prompt; `paneDialogState` already reports that in the `202`
370	(`parked_on`, `suspicious_dialog`) and still does not refuse. That limit is the same
371	one spec 018 recorded, and closing it needs a readiness signal this daemon does not
372	have yet.
373	
374	Also out of this feature by the same reasoning: **the Go code never opens a Claude
375	transcript or a `~/.claude/sessions/*.json` registry file.** Spec 013 FR-025 is
376	unchanged by this feature, and spec 019 D11's bounded Codex rollout read stays the
377	single exception it already is.
378	
379	---
380	
381	## D9 Out of scope
382	
383	**Decision.** This feature does not do any of the following, and a task that finds
384	itself needing one stops rather than widening:
385	
386	| Not done here | Why |
387	|---|---|
388	| Opening a transcript | Spec 013 FR-025 (D8) |
389	| Holding or calling an LLM | The daemon routes keystrokes; it does not reason about them |
390	| A seventh API route | The API door has exactly six (Code: `internal/httpapi/server.go`'s route switch; six `## <METHOD> <path>` headings in `specs/001-crswd-daemon-core/contracts/http-api.md`). Requirements 1 to 6 are all changes to one existing route |
391	| Free text on the browser door beyond spec 018 | Spec 018 owns that panel; D5 touches its route only to assert it is unchanged |
392	| The startup lost-Enter window | Probe check 1b: an Enter can be lost in the first ~5 s after launch. Two liveness reads around the paste do not see it, and closing it needs a start-up readiness signal (D8) |
393	| The socket transport | The probe's verdict ("flip to socket") binds the lm-steer-write milestone, not this one |
394	| A new package under `internal/` | Every change lands in `audit`, `httpapi`, `session` or `tmuxctl` |
395	
396	The last two rows are also hard rules of the loop that implements this spec, and the
397	validation contract asserts the `internal/` one by diffing the tree against `main`.
398	
399	---
400	
401	## Not verified
402	
403	Stated so that a later reader does not mistake any of these for a settled fact:
404	
405	- Whether a pane can fall back to a shell *between* the second liveness read and the
406	  Enter. The window is two tmux commands wide and nothing measured it; the `C-u` of D2
407	  covers the measured case (an exit during the paste) and not this one.
408	- Whether `LivenessUnknown` ever appears for a session this daemon created. It is
409	  reachable only for a session created before `@crswd-binary` existed, and no such
410	  session was on the probe host.
411	- What a Codex session does with a prompt refused after its paste. `C-u` clears a
412	  Claude composer and a shell line; Codex's composer was not measured against it.
413	- Whether any non-lawnmower client of this route exists. The grep covered ai-lawnmower
414	  only, so D5's "no existing caller is refused" is a statement about that client.
415

# Research: prompt route safety

**Spec**: [spec.md](spec.md) · **Plan**: [plan.md](plan.md) · **Tasks**: [tasks.md](tasks.md)

This feature hardens `POST /sessions/{id}/prompt`, the one API route that already
delivers free text into a running session. It is the route ai-lawnmower's `answer`
and opp-lease handoff call today, so every change here is a change to a live client.

## Where the evidence comes from

Three sources, and each decision below says which one it leans on.

| Tag | Source | Status |
|---|---|---|
| **Probe** | `~/code/ai-lawnmower/ralph/plans/lm-steer-design/results.md`, numbered checks | Outside this repo, read-only. The checks this feature turns on are transcribed into `ralph/plans/lm-steer-crswd-018/PROGRESS.md` ("Probe results that decide this plan") because the loop that implements this spec cannot reach that path |
| **Design** | `~/code/ai-lawnmower/docs/mcp-session-steering-design.md`, section (g) "Phase 3 detail" | Outside this repo, read-only. It is where requirements 1 to 7 are stated |
| **Code** | This repository at `30941f3` | Read and re-read in tree on 10/14/26; the line references below were checked, not remembered |

The decisions were taken during planning, before any task ran, and are recorded in
`ralph/plans/lm-steer-crswd-018/IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md` under "Decisions already
made". They are reproduced here with their evidence. **They are not reopened by the
implementation**; a task that finds one of them wrong stops and says so rather than
choosing differently.

## The route as it stands (Code, 10/14/26)

What the hardening is measured against:

- `internal/httpapi/sessions.go` `promptSession` (line 772) decodes `promptRequest`,
  best-effort-reads the pane for a known dialog (`paneDialogState`, which is
  additive information and never a gate), calls `Manager.Prompt`, and answers `202`
  with `{"id","delivered","parked_on","suspicious_dialog"}`.
- `refusePrompt` (line 849) maps `session.ErrEmptyPrompt` to `400` and **everything
  else to a `500` with no detail**. There is no 409 on this route today.
- `internal/session/manager.go` `Manager.Prompt` (line 1194) refuses an empty ID
  (`ErrSessionNotFound`), `StateDead` (`ErrSessionDead`) and empty text
  (`ErrEmptyPrompt`); takes `lockSession`; calls `m.paste`; then `SendKeys` Enter.
- `m.paste` (line 1253) is bracketed **only** when the harness spec says
  `BracketedPaste`, which Claude's does not (spec 019 D9 left that to spec 018, and
  spec 018 FR-006 declined it for the API door).
- `Manager.Prompt` does **not** read liveness, does **not** consult `StateFailed`,
  and does **not** take the restart claim.

So a prompt into a session whose Claude has exited lands in a login shell as a
command line, and a prompt racing a revival lands half in one process and half in
the next. Those are the two failures this feature closes.

---

## D1 Spec number

**Decision.** This feature is `specs/020-prompt-route-safety/`.

**Evidence.** The design calls it "crswd spec 018", but `specs/018-interactive-input`
(the session page's input panel) and `specs/019-codex-runtime` already exist in this
repository (Code: `ls specs/`). 020 is the first free number.

The milestone directory keeps the design's name — `ralph/plans/lm-steer-crswd-018/` —
because the lawnmower side refers to it that way. The mismatch is deliberate and is
stated in `VALIDATION_CONTRACT.md` so that a later reader does not "fix" one to match
the other.

---

## D2 Liveness gate (requirement 1)

**Decision.** `Manager.Prompt` reads the session's row from the controller's `List`
and branches on its `Claude` liveness:

- `LivenessStopped` → refuse with `ErrSessionNotReady`, before any tmux command that
  changes anything.
- `LivenessUnknown` → deliver.
- `LivenessRunning` → deliver.
- A `List` that fails → an error, not a delivery.

The gate runs **twice**: once before the paste, and again after the paste and before
the Enter. If the second read is stopped, the daemon sends `C-u` and no Enter.

**Evidence.**

- Probe check 13: `@crswd-binary` matched `pane_current_command` on 6 of 6 live panes,
  three of them `rcq` panes. So the option the daemon already sets is a true liveness
  signal for the sessions lawnmower actually drives, not only for the plain case.
- Code: `tmuxctl.SessionInfo.Claude` is the three-valued `Liveness`
  (`internal/tmuxctl/controller.go:312-341`), derived from `@crswd-binary` against the
  pane's current command — by one tmux format in `Exec` (`exec.go:548`) and by
  `livenessOf` in the fake (`fake.go:251`). Both exist already; nothing new is
  measured here.
- Spec 012 FR-006 ("detect a session whose Claude process has stopped while its shell
  survives") is the requirement this reads, and `supervisor.go:153-156` already treats
  `LivenessUnknown` as healthy with a comment saying it must. This gate reads it the
  same way, so a session created before `@crswd-binary` existed keeps working.
- Probe check 1: there is no check-then-Enter race after the first turn; the lost-Enter
  window is the first ~5 s after launch, which is out of scope (D9). That is why two
  reads around the paste are enough and a third is not.

**Why `List` and not a new method.** A per-session liveness method on
`tmuxctl.Controller` would force a matching change in the k8s module's `podctl`
(Code: `k8s/` is a second module reaching the root's `internal/` through `replace ../`).
This milestone adds no `Controller` method, so `podctl` is untouched and the cluster
build does not move.

**Why the second read, and why `C-u`.** Between the paste and the Enter the pane can
fall back to a shell — Claude exits, the composer's text is gone, and the Enter would
submit whatever the paste left on the shell's line as a command. `C-u` clears that
line; sending no Enter means nothing runs. Refusing *after* a paste is not as good as
refusing before one, and the `C-u` is what makes the imperfect case harmless rather
than merely reported.

*Rejected: refusing `LivenessUnknown`.* It is the state of every session started by a
build older than the option, and refusing it would make this route stop working for
sessions the supervisor itself calls healthy — two answers to one question.

*Rejected: reading the pane's text to decide readiness.* Spec 012 FR-007 forbids it
for detection, pane content is secret under `docs/security.md` §3, and `paneDialogState`
already shows what a text read is good for: additive information, never a gate.

---

## D3 Not-ready answer (requirements 1, 2 and 5)

**Decision.** One new sentinel, `session.ErrSessionNotReady`. Every refusal this
feature adds inside `internal/session` returns it, and `refusePrompt` maps it to
`409` with body `{"error":"session not ready"}` and an audit **Deny** whose reason is
the constant `session not ready`.

A session in `StateFailed` gets it. `StateDead` keeps today's answer unchanged.

**Evidence.**

- Code: `StateFailed` (`internal/session/session.go:86`) means the supervisor tried to
  bring the session back and ran out of attempts (`supervisor.go:311-314`). Nothing is
  running in that pane, so a prompt into it is the same failure as a stopped pane;
  `Manager.Prompt` refuses `StateDead` today and says nothing about `StateFailed`.
- Code: a dead session is already refused as a `404` by the resolver before
  `promptSession` runs, and `refusePrompt`'s comment says reaching its `ErrSessionDead`
  branch would mean a record went terminal between two layers of one request. Leaving
  `dead` alone keeps that path exactly as it is and keeps the enumeration rule
  (`docs/security.md`: a session the caller may not have is a 404, never a 403/409).
- lawnmower's `deliver()` (`~/code/ai-lawnmower/loop/session_resume.py`, as recorded in
  PROGRESS.md on 10/14/26) treats **any** body carrying an `error` key as a refusal. So
  `409 {"error":"session not ready"}` reads as a refusal to the existing client with no
  client change, which is why the body carries `error` and not a new key.
- `docs/security.md` "Rate limiting & audit": every reason on the trail is a sentinel
  this codebase authored. `session not ready` is one. It names no state, no pane
  content and no prompt — an operator reading the trail learns that the route refused
  and why in the daemon's own words, and a caller learns nothing about the host it
  could not already see.

*Rejected: a sentinel per reason* (stopped pane, failed state, restart held). Three
sentinels reaching one status code with one body is three things to keep in step for
a distinction the caller cannot observe. The trail distinguishes nothing more here
because the three are the same event to the client: not now, try later.

*Rejected: `503`.* The condition is about one named session, not about this daemon's
capacity, and `409` is already the contract's "the host's state refuses this" code
(the unverified-teardown answer, `sessions.go:749`).

---

## D4 Bracketed paste (requirement 3)

**Decision.** `Manager.Prompt` pastes with `PasteBracketed` for **every** harness.
`Manager.Compact` keeps its harness-based paste (`m.paste`). No newline refusal.

**Evidence.**

- Code: `Controller.PasteBracketed` already exists (spec 018 added it; `paste-buffer -p`,
  `internal/tmuxctl/exec.go:220-230`), and the session page's type route already uses it
  for every harness. This decision reuses that method; it adds none.
- `docs/security.md` §2: inside a bracketed paste the terminal does not interpret the
  pasted bytes, which is what makes multi-line text one paste instead of a line of text
  plus a submit plus another line. The same section already requires that caller text
  reach tmux only through `load-buffer` on stdin and then `paste-buffer`, bracketed on
  the session page's route; this extends the bracketing to the API door's route.
- Spec 019 D9 / research M3–M5 measured that Codex swallows the Enter after a *plain*
  paste and submits correctly after a bracketed one. Claude accepts both. So bracketed
  is the one form that is correct for both harnesses, and `Prompt` stops needing to ask
  which harness it is talking to at all.
**A consequence this decision does not close, named rather than smoothed over.**
`docs/security.md` §2 says text holding a C0 control other than TAB or LF is refused,
"because inside a bracketed paste `ESC[201~` would end the paste" — and that sentence
is about **the session page's route**. The refusal is `session.ValidateTyped`
(`internal/session/input.go:75-92`, spec 018 FR-004), and Code confirms it is called by
`Manager.Type` (`input.go:105`) and **not** by `Manager.Prompt`: the API door's
`promptRequest.Text` is validated only for emptiness and the body-size bound
(`internal/httpapi/sessions.go:264-270`, "that is the whole of its validation
(FR-030)"). So bracketing this route's paste makes a byte sequence relevant that was
inert under a plain paste: a caller that sent `\x1b[201~` mid-text would end the paste
early and the remainder would reach the pane as keystrokes rather than as pasted text.

D4 as decided adds no refusal, so this feature does not close it, and this document
does not invent one. What is recorded here is that the mechanism already exists
(`ValidateTyped`, one call away) and that spec.md has to say which way it goes —
either the route gains that check or the exposure is accepted in writing. It is logged
as a finding in `ralph/plans/lm-steer-crswd-018/PROGRESS.md` so the task that writes
spec.md cannot miss it. No measured client sends a control byte: every fixture in
PROGRESS.md "Payload fixtures" is printable text plus newlines.

**Why no newline refusal.** The opp-lease handoff pastes multi-line item bodies
(Probe/Design: the builders in `console.py` and `lawnmower-route`, whose shapes are
fixed byte-for-byte as T011's fixtures in PROGRESS.md "Payload fixtures"). A rule
refusing `\n` would refuse the traffic this route exists to carry. Bracketing is what
makes a newline safe; refusing newlines would be the same protection obtained by
breaking the client.

**Why `Compact` is untouched.** Its payload is a daemon constant, not caller text, and
spec 018 FR-006's "unchanged" promise about this route is amended here only for what
requirements 1 to 6 name. Changing `Compact` as well would be an unrequested change to
a path with no requirement behind it (constitution IV).

This amends spec 018 **FR-006**, which says the API door's prompt route must be
unchanged — plain paste, then Enter, with bracketed paste reserved for the interactive
route. The amendment is recorded in spec.md, not left to this file.

---

## D5 Leading `!` or `/` (requirement 4)

**Decision.** On the **API door only**: refuse a prompt whose first character that is
not space, tab, CR or LF is `!` or `/`. The answer is `400` with the uniform
bad-request body, decided before any tmux command runs. The session page's type route
is unchanged.

**Evidence.**

- Design, requirement 4: those two characters are Claude Code's slash-command and
  shell-escape prefixes. A prompt that begins with one is not a prompt — `/clear`
  discards the conversation the caller was trying to continue, and `!` runs a shell
  command in the session's own unsandboxed context. A client that meant to say
  something and instead silently reset the session is the failure being closed.
- Code grep of 10/14/26 over every lawnmower caller of this route: `console.py`
  `_answer_action` (via `session_resume.deliver`), `lawnmower-route` `resume_prompt`,
  `_batch_listing_prompt`, and `opp_followup_prompt` all build text whose first
  character is a letter. **No existing caller is refused by this rule.** That is the
  whole of why it can be added to a live route at all.
- The fixtures in PROGRESS.md keep the shape that matters: `resume.txt` holds a *later*
  line beginning `/compact`. The rule is about the first non-whitespace character of
  the whole text and nothing else, so that fixture is accepted. A rule scanning every
  line would refuse real traffic.
- The browser door is excluded because its route is the operator typing at their own
  session: `docs/security.md` records the session page's input panel as text or a key
  the operator sent, delivered once, when they pressed it. An operator typing
  `/compact` into their own session is the feature, not a mistake, and T004 asserts
  that it still arrives.

*Rejected: stripping or escaping the leading character.* It would deliver something
the caller did not write, into a session that executes code. A refusal the client can
see and fix is strictly better than a silent rewrite.

*Rejected: an allowlist of safe slash commands.* The daemon would then own a list that
tracks Claude Code's command set, and a stale list is a command delivered because
nobody updated a table. The route carries prompts; a caller that wants a command has
the browser door and the operator behind it.

This amends spec 018 **FR-006** a second time (see D4): the route gains one refusal
the interactive route does not have.

---

## D6 Lock and buffer (requirement 5)

**Decision.** `Manager.Prompt` takes the restart claim (`claimRestart`, non-blocking)
**after** `lockSession`, refuses with `ErrSessionNotReady` when a revive or a continue
already holds it, and releases it on return.

**Evidence.**

- Code: `lockSession` (`internal/session/input.go`) is already the per-session mutex
  shared by Type, PressKey, Prompt, Compact, SetMode, Continue, Destroy and the
  supervisor's Codex discovery. `Prompt` already takes it (`manager.go:1209`), so two
  concurrent prompts already cannot interleave paste and Enter.
- Code: `Exec.paste` already draws a fresh buffer name per paste (`newBufferName`,
  `exec.go:186-195`, 16 random hex digits behind `BufferPrefix`, "per call rather than
  per session, so a second paste into the same session cannot overwrite the first
  one's text before it lands"). The fake records the names through `nextBuffer`, so a
  test can assert they differ. Both halves of requirement 5's "distinct buffers, no
  interleaving" are therefore **already true**, from the spec 018 and 019 review
  passes, and this feature only has to prove it (T010) rather than build it.
- Code: `claimRestart` / `releaseRestart` (`manager.go:2674-2688`) are non-blocking and
  are what revival and continue hold while they type a new command line into the pane.
  That is the one concurrent writer `lockSession` does **not** exclude, because a
  restart does not hold the session lock for its whole run. A prompt pasted into a pane
  mid-restart lands partly in the dying process and partly on the shell the new command
  line is about to be typed at.

**Why non-blocking.** A prompt that waited for a revival would hold an HTTP request
open across a process restart, and the caller cannot tell a slow delivery from a lost
one. `409 session not ready` is a fact the client can act on now; lawnmower's
`deliver()` already reads it as a refusal (D3).

**Why after `lockSession` and not before.** The two are taken in one order everywhere
or they deadlock. `lockSession` first matches `Continue`'s order, so no new ordering
rule enters the package.

---

## D7 `request_id` (requirement 6)

**Decision.** The prompt body gains one optional field, `request_id`: 1 to 32
characters of `[a-z0-9-]`. A value outside that is a `400`. A valid value is echoed in
the `202` body and written as `request_id` on the request's one audit record. Absent
means the field appears nowhere — not in the response, not on the record.

**Evidence.**

- Design, requirement 6: the caller needs to correlate a delivery it made with the
  record of that delivery, across a daemon restart and without a transcript. The audit
  trail is the only durable record of a prompt, and today it carries nothing the caller
  chose.
- Code: `audit.Record` (`internal/audit/audit.go:390-414`) has Action, Caller,
  SessionID, Decision, Reason and Remote. `RequestAudit`
  (`internal/httpapi/middleware.go`) has `SetSessionID` and `Deny`, so the
  carry-it-onto-the-one-record mechanism exists and gains one setter (T002) rather
  than a second record.
- The value goes in a **field of its own** and never into `Reason`. `Record.Reason`'s
  own documentation forbids caller-supplied text in it ("must never be built from
  caller-supplied text, a prompt, pane output, a token, or the shared secret"), and
  that rule is unamended: `Reason` stays server-authored sentinels, and `request_id`
  is the one field on the record whose bytes the caller chose.
- `docs/security.md` §2 and the decoder it shows: the body is decoded into a typed
  struct with `DisallowUnknownFields`, so the field has to be declared to be accepted
  at all, and anything else in the body is still refused.

**Why that alphabet and that length.** The field is written to an audit record that an
operator reads and a tool greps. Lower-case, digits and `-` is the same shape this
repository already holds session names to (`^[a-zA-Z0-9-]{1,64}$`, `docs/security.md`
§2), minus the upper case; 32 characters fits a ULID or a UUID and leaves nothing for
a caller to smuggle. Validation is at the boundary and the refusal is a `400`, so no
tmux command runs for a body that was never going to be accepted.

**Why this is not a hole in FR-042.** Spec 001 FR-042 forbids prompt text, session
output, credentials and the shared secret on an audit record, and nothing in it
contemplated a caller-chosen correlation value. This amends FR-042 for **this one
field**, and the bound is exact: the record gains the `request_id` the caller sent and
**nothing about the prompt** — not its text, not its length, not a hash of it. The
alphabet is what keeps the field from becoming a channel for the text itself: 32 bytes
of `[a-z0-9-]` cannot carry a prompt, and a caller that tried would be writing a value
an operator can see is not an identifier. The amendment is recorded in spec.md.

---

## D8 Registry gate (requirement 7) — deferred, not a clarification

**Decision.** Requirement 7, a readiness gate reading Claude Code's session registry,
is **out of scope** for this feature. It is listed under Out of scope in spec.md with
this reason. It is **not** an open question in constitution II's sense — a deferred
MAY is a decision, and the marker that principle calls for is deliberately absent
from this directory. (Spelling that marker out here would also trip the gate that
greps this directory for it, which is why no file under `specs/020-prompt-route-safety/`
contains the phrase.)

**Evidence.**

- The design states requirement 7 as a **MAY**, not a MUST. Deferring a MAY is a scope
  decision, not an unanswered question, and constitution II is about requirements that
  are *ambiguous* — this one is clear and declined.
- Probe check 8 left open whether crswd can read `sessions/<pid>.json` at all under
  spec 017's v2 option B. No FR in spec 017 places that file in a pod, so a gate built
  on it would work on the VM and silently do nothing in the cluster — a readiness check
  that is right about one deployment and blind in the other.
- Probe checks 3 and 9: the registry misses the trust dialog and misses a half-typed
  draft in the composer. So it answers "a session exists" and not "this session will
  read what I send next", which is the question requirement 7 was asked to answer.
- The liveness gate (D2) is the part of requirement 1 that is measurable with what the
  daemon already holds, and it is what ships.

**What this costs, stated rather than smoothed over.** A session sitting on a dialog
still accepts a prompt; `paneDialogState` already reports that in the `202`
(`parked_on`, `suspicious_dialog`) and still does not refuse. That limit is the same
one spec 018 recorded, and closing it needs a readiness signal this daemon does not
have yet.

Also out of this feature by the same reasoning: **the Go code never opens a Claude
transcript or a `~/.claude/sessions/*.json` registry file.** Spec 013 FR-025 is
unchanged by this feature, and spec 019 D11's bounded Codex rollout read stays the
single exception it already is.

---

## D9 Out of scope

**Decision.** This feature does not do any of the following, and a task that finds
itself needing one stops rather than widening:

| Not done here | Why |
|---|---|
| Opening a transcript | Spec 013 FR-025 (D8) |
| Holding or calling an LLM | The daemon routes keystrokes; it does not reason about them |
